<!-- Custom floating TOC container -->
<nav id="floating-toc" aria-label="Table of contents">
  <div class="toc-title">Contents</div>

<script>
// Build a TOC from H2/H3 headings (skip the hero H1)
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function(){
  var list = document.getElementById('floating-toc-list');
  if (!list) return;
  var headings = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('h2, h3'));
  headings = headings.filter(function(h){ return !h.closest('.toc-ignore'); });
  headings.forEach(function(h){
    if (!h.id) {
      var id = h.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[^\w]+/g,'-').replace(/(^-|-$)/g,'');
      if (!id) id = 'section-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,8);
      var base = id, k = 2;
      while (document.getElementById(id)) { id = base + '-' + k++; }
      h.id = id;
    }
    var li = document.createElement('li');
    if (h.tagName === 'H3') li.className = 'h3';
    var a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = '#' + h.id;
    a.textContent = h.textContent;
    li.appendChild(a);
    list.appendChild(li);
  });
});
</script>

## Brief Bio

---

Hien Nguyen holds dual positions as an Associate Professor at La Trobe University in Australia and a Professor at the Institute of Mathematics for Industry at Kyushu University in Japan. His role focuses on building collaborative relationships between the two institutions and the two countries at large to foster new innovative research in mathematical and computational statistics, as well as the applications of such developments. Hien also holds an Honorary Associate Professorship at his Alma Mater, the University of Queensland in Brisbane, Australia, where he continues to supervise students.

Hien has a strong interest in the research of computational statistics and its interaction with the fields of machine learning and AI. His research focuses on the analysis of large datasets that are acquired incrementally or are too large for conventional computers. In such settings, his work centres on the use of methods such as stochastic optimisation theory and Bayesian inference to handle such difficulties. He is also interested in the development of rigorous statistical tools for choosing between models when data are complex and for testing the validity of such choices, as well as providing confidence statements regarding the goodness of inferential decisions in practice.

Hien's methods have found applications in multiple areas of applied research, including neuroimaging, agriculture, genetics and genomics, proteomics, quantum computing, economics, public policy, and social sciences. Outside of his work, Hien Nguyen currently holds editorial roles with the *Australian and New Zealand Journal of Statistics*, *Heliyon Mathematics*, the *International Journal of Mathematics for Industry*, and *Statistical Analysis and Data Mining*.

In his free time, Hien Nguyen enjoys bushwalking and spending time with his three cats: Nyx, Penelope, and Beau.

### Roles

* Professor at the Institute of Mathematics for Industry, Kyushu University in Fukuoka, Japan (2023–Present)
* Associate Professor at La Trobe University in Melbourne, Australia (2023–Present)
* Honorary Associate Professor at the University of Queensland in Brisbane, Australia (2023–Present)
* Executive Editor of *Statistical Analysis and Data Mining* (2024–Present)
* Associate Editor of *Heliyon Mathematics* (2026-Present)
* Associate Editor of the *International Journal of Mathematics for Industry* (2024–Present)
* Book Review Editor of the *Australian and New Zealand Journal of Statistics* (2023–Present)
* Technical Editor of the *Australian and New Zealand Journal of Statistics* (2018–Present)

### Major Projects
**Australia’s Economic Accelerator (AEA) Innovate Program IV240100099 (with Aniruddha Desai, Krishnakumar Santhanam, Lalit Yagnik, Mark Jois, Erik van Vulpen, Aidin Bervan, Shanmuga Sundar Dhanabalan, and Phat Huynh): Fully integrated digital technology solution for enhanced dairy farm management.**

*2025–2027*

* This project develops a fully integrated digital technology solution for enhanced dairy farm management.

**ARC DP250100860 (with Shu-Kay Angus Ng, Griffith University; Florence Forbes, Inria; Liming Xiang, Nanyang Technological University): Advancing statistical models for clustering data with structured dependence.**

*2025–2027*

* This project develops statistical models and algorithms for clustering data with structured dependence.

**STARFISH Activity (with Rebecca Chisholm, Mark Davies, Tim Barnett, David Price, Trish Campbell, and Joel Miller): Optimising targeted investigations of Strep A transmission and Environmental Health Initiatives (EHIs) assessment: a model-based approach.**

*2024–2026*

* This project develops model-based methods for targeted investigations of Strep A transmission and Environmental Health Initiatives assessment.

**Inria Associate Teams WOMBAT (with Florence Forbes, Inria): Variance-reduced Optimization Methods and Bayesian Approximation Techniques for scalable inference.**

*2023–2026*

* This project develops variance-reduced optimisation methods and Bayesian approximation techniques for scalable inference.

**ARC DP230100905 (with Xin Guo, University of Queensland; Florence Forbes, Inria; Gersende Fort, CNRS): Stochastic majorization–minimization algorithms for data science.**

*2023–2025*

* This project develops stochastic majorization–minimization algorithms for large-scale data science problems.

### Past Projects

**Australian Government Road Safety Innovation Fund (with Long Truong, La Trobe University): Development of planning-stage crash prediction tools for use at the planning stages.**

*2021–2023*

* This project developed planning-stage crash prediction tools for use in transport planning.

**Inria Associate Teams LANDER (with Florence Forbes, Inria): Latent analysis, adversarial networks, and DimEnsionality Reduction.**

*2019–2021*

* This project supported collaborative work on latent analysis, adversarial networks, and dimensionality reduction.

**ARC DP180101192 (with Geoffrey McLachlan, University of Queensland; and Sharon Lee, University of Queensland): Classification methods for providing personalised and class decisions.**

*2018–2021*

* This project developed classification methods for providing personalised and class decisions.

**ARC DE170101134: Feasible algorithms for big inference.**

*2017–2020*

* This project developed feasible algorithms for big inference.

<style>
  .self-name { color: var(--accent); font-weight: 700; }
</style>

<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
  // Match variants of your name in APA outputs
  const patterns = [
    /\bNguyen,\s*H\.?\s*D\.?\b/g,        // "Nguyen, H. D."
    /\bNguyen,\s*H\.?(?!\s*[A-Z])/g,     // "Nguyen, H" (not followed by another initial)
    /\bNguyen,\s*Hien\s*D(?:uy)?\.?\b/g, // "Nguyen, Hien D." or "Nguyen, Hien Duy"
    /\bHien\s+Duy\s+Nguyen\b/g           // "Hien Duy Nguyen"
  ];

  const refs = document.querySelectorAll('#refs .csl-entry, .references .csl-entry');
  refs.forEach(p => {
    let html = p.innerHTML;
    // Unwrap any previous runs to prevent nesting
    html = html.replace(/<(?:strong|span)\s+class=["']self-name["']>([^<]+)<\/(?:strong|span)>/g, '$1');
    // Wrap matches in a span we can style
    patterns.forEach(rx => {
      html = html.replace(rx, m => '<span class="self-name">' + m + '</span>');
    });
    p.innerHTML = html;
  });
});
</script>
